title: Argument-refusal marker blocks later same-key admission when a deeper reported directory makes relative arguments valid
outcome: A later start reporting a changed directory can admit an honest Unknown check when the command's relative arguments become contained, while duplicate argument-refusal notices remain controlled.
acceptance: The lifecycle distinguishes duplicate refusals from changed placement that makes previously rejected relative arguments valid, preserving conservative guards and Unknown attribution for late admission.
A regression drives first argument-refused start followed by a valid same-key start with changed cwd, and verifies one honest Unknown check without passing credit.
The full five-stage gate passes on the exact committed tree.
